newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy pension spending out of kilter - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy pension spending out of kilter - Prodi.

text.p: Italian state spending on pensions is some 15 trillion lire a year over budget and needs bringing into line, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in an interview with La Repubblica on Friday.

Prodi's centre-left government on Wednesday opened talks with the leaders of Italy's three main unions and employers' group Confindustria on the thorny question of reforms of the welfare state and the pension system.
The powerful unions have already indicated they are opposed to cuts in pensions, but Prodi said social spending was unbalanced.

Asked by La Repubblica if the government was seeking 15 trillion lire a year in cuts, Prodi replied: "Pension spending will be out of line by 1.5 percent a year over the next three years. And this 1.5 percent corresponds more or less to that figure there.
"(But) there is no massacre in sight. Here we are seeking to prevent the system from exploding," he added.
"We are looking to re-balance (spending), no-one wants spending to be cut. The objective...is to stabilise spending against gross domestic product at average levels for 1996-97," Prodi said.
Talks over welfare reform will carry on uninterrupted until September, Prodi said.
Italy is under pressure to carry out a convincing reform of social spending to prove that public finances will be kept under control before the planned 1999 launch of the single European currency.
